skill.name: generating-storyboards
skill.description: Creates one 16:9 storyboard sheet per video clip, with vertical panels that show one action each. It uses supplied references and prior sheets to maintain person, product, setting, and story continuity.
skill.summary: Create consistent storyboard sheets from a settled video plan and visual references.
skill.author: supercmohq

content.value_statement: Video concepts can lose continuity when clips are planned separately. This skill creates sequential storyboard sheets that preserve characters, products, settings, and visual states.
actual_capabilities: Creates one 16:9 storyboard sheet for each planned video clip.
Divides clip actions into vertical panels based on a two-to-four-second rhythm.
Analyzes supplied person, product, and setting references before planning panels.
Writes image-generation prompts with camera, framing, action, hand, product, and performance details.
Uses each completed sheet as a reference for continuity in the next sheet.
Handles pending image jobs and common reference-count or provider errors.
limitations: Requires a settled clip story, duration, sheet count, and relevant visual references.
Generates static storyboard sheets, not animated video or standalone still-image concepts.
Builds sheets sequentially because each later sheet depends on the previous result.
Cannot guarantee exact text, anatomy, product details, or identity from an image model.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Demonstration
use_cases.description: Turn a timed product story into panels with realistic handling, camera changes, and consistent product presentation.

use_cases.title: Previsualize a Social Video
use_cases.description: Create sequential sheets that show actions, expressions, framing, and continuity before filming or generation.

use_cases.title: Review Visual Continuity
use_cases.description: Check how a person, wardrobe, setting, and object states carry across multiple planned clips.

prompt_templates.title: Create One Storyboard Sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Create storyboard sheet 1 of 1 for a [duration]-second clip where [action]. Use the supplied [person or product] reference and a [look] style.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one settled clip and the required references.

prompt_templates.title: Storyboard a Product Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Build sheet [number] of [total] for a [duration]-second product clip. The subject [story]. Use the supplied person and product references. Preserve the product size and visible face.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product video needs realistic handling and presentation.

prompt_templates.title: Continue a Multi-Clip Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create sheet [number] of [total] from the supplied person, product, and previous-sheet references. Continue [carryover state], then deliberately change [planned change] during this [duration]-second clip.
prompt_templates.scenario: Several clips must preserve visual and narrative continuity.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Complex Action Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Storyboard sheet [number] of [total] for [duration] seconds. The story includes [actions]. Split it into feasible panels, identify any action that does not fit, and preserve [continuity constraints] from the previous sheet.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs action decomposition and continuity checks.

output_examples.input: Create a six-second sheet where the subject picks up a jar and turns its label toward the camera.
output_examples.output: A 16:9 sheet with two vertical panels: first, a medium shot of the pickup; second, a close shot of the label turn.

output_examples.input: Continue the next clip as the subject opens the product and applies it.
output: Carryover: the same subject, wardrobe, setting, light, and product position from the previous sheet.
Panel 1 shows the product already open after the cut.
Panel 2 shows one clear application action with suitable framing and hand use.

output_examples.input: Storyboard four actions inside a five-second clip.
output_examples.output: The response explains that four distinct actions exceed the available panel rhythm and recommends removing or moving actions.

best_practices: Provide the final clip story, duration, sheet count, and intended visual look.
Supply clear person and product references, with product dimensions when relevant.
Review each generated sheet before using it as the next sheet's continuity reference.
anti_patterns: Do not request all sheets in parallel because later sheets require the previous image.
Do not assign several primary actions to one panel or crowd a short clip.
Do not describe identity traits that conflict with the supplied person reference.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates one 16:9 storyboard sheet per video clip, using vertical panels arranged from left to right.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the clip story, duration, sheet number, total sheets, visual look, and relevant person or product references.

faq.question: Can it generate every sheet at once?
faq.answer: No. It creates sheets sequentially because each later prompt uses the previous sheet as a continuity reference.

faq.question: How does it choose the number of panels?
faq.answer: It assigns one primary action per panel and targets approximately two to four seconds of clip time per panel.

faq.question: Does it generate the finished video?
faq.answer: No. It produces static storyboard sheets for review before filming, animation, or video generation.

faq.question: How does it maintain consistency?
faq.answer: It labels visual references, locks unchanged details, tracks object states, and passes each completed sheet into the next generation.
